html:
The Varangian Guard was the bodyguard of the Byzantine emperors from the late 10th to the 14th century, made up of warriors from northern Europe. Its members were famous for their great axes and their loyalty to whoever held the throne.

It grew out of the 6,000 warriors that Prince Vladimir of Kiev sent to Basil II around 988, in a deal that also brought the baptism of Rus'. Varangian was the Greek name for the Norse. Many came from Scandinavia by the rivers of Russia, and service in Constantinople was a way to get rich; runestones in Sweden remember men who died "in Greece". The most famous recruit was Harald Hardrada, who served in the 1030s and 1040s before he became king of Norway.

After the Norman conquest of England in 1066 many Anglo-Saxons joined, and the guard became largely English. They fought the Normans at the Battle of Dyrrhachium in 1081 and defended the walls against the crusaders in 1203 and 1204. The unit fades from the record in the 14th century.
